prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional PROTAC molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation meets my own standard of a game-changer with real consequences. It is a new kind of chemistry: a small molecule is designed to bring a target and an E3 ligase together so the protein is removed rather than merely inhibited. That opens targets that were considered undruggable. Six of eight of us ranked it, five in the top three, and the mechanism has been confirmed in many independent laboratories. The principle is simple, in the spirit of not overcomplicating matters, and it is quantitative: ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design and structure-guided ligands such as the VHL ligands can all be measured and explained. Crews and Deshaies supply the founding concept and proof of principle, and Ciulli supplies the structural and rational-design work that made degraders drug-like. That is a coherent three-person story, and it leaves a clear citation.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet an approved drug, so the clinical consequences are still prospective and recognition could look early. A larger problem is attribution. The molecular-glue branch (Handa and Ito on cereblon, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim) is a different mechanistic strand that a Crews/Deshaies/Ciulli prize would leave out, and a three-name limit forces an arguable cut. If the committee judges that the glue and PROTAC strands are one achievement, my trio is weaker than I have been treating it.

responses.point: Chabes prefers Handa in the third place, because identifying cereblon as the thalidomide target explains the molecular-glue branch and enabled the CRBN-based degraders.
responses.response: I take the cereblon discovery seriously. It is a mechanistic breakthrough and arguably the reason degraders reached the clinic so quickly. But it is a discovery about how an existing drug works, while the PROTAC concept is a design principle that works for any target. The prize should reward the generalizable chemistry. I keep Ciulli because the VHL ligands and the ternary-complex structures turned the idea into rational design. I would accept a Handa version if the committee agrees that the molecular-glue strand is the center of gravity, but I would want to see that argued rather than assumed.

responses.point: Linke ranks phase separation first, as a clear physical principle with quantitative support that organizes cell chemistry, and he ranks degraders second, with the concern that the molecular glues complicate attribution.
responses.response: I agree with Heiner on the attribution problem for degraders, and my answer to it is above. On phase separation I am less convinced. The founding observations of liquid-like P granules are well documented, but I am not yet persuaded that most in-cell condensates are genuine phase separation rather than overexpression artifacts, and I do not see a quantitative link to experiment as clear as the degrader mechanism has. That is a question of maturity, not of quality. I would like to hear which of the physiological claims he regards as settled.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling first. It is a mature, general, industrially routine method, and he treats Hartwig and Buchwald as a clean pair with Kosugi as precursor.
responses.response: The attribution here is cleaner than for almost any other candidate, and the maturity case is stronger than for degraders. Nothing about the science is in doubt. My reservation is the one I would raise about the 2010 cross-coupling prize: the committee would need to say why C-N coupling is a new idea and not an extension of a recognised class. Peter's point that it made a hard transformation routine is a fair answer, so I place it as a serious alternative to degraders rather than a lesser one, though I still rank degraders higher on novelty.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first and nitrogenase second, valuing quantitative physical mechanism and four decades of confirmation.
responses.response: I share Peter's preference for work that is quantitative and tested against experiment, and Gray and Winkler's tunnelling work meets that. My difficulty is the same as his: Marcus theory was recognised in 1992, so the prize would be about the biological extension, and the question is whether that is a game-changer or a deepening of a recognised one. I find that a harder case to make than degraders, though I do not dismiss it.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats PROTACs and molecular glue degraders as one achievement or two, and so whether Handa and Ito must be accommodated.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes recognition premature this year.
Whether Ciulli or Handa is the better third name, given the three-person limit.
How the committee weighs the maturity of C-N coupling or sequencing against the novelty of degraders.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. My connection to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome community does not touch any shortlisted laureate. I have no known tie to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa or the others on the degrader ballot.
